title: Reading Key Levels
hook: Clear Level Detective, pass the Knowledge Check, save your Check-In, then pass the Phase 2 Final to complete Understanding Structure.

game.title: Level Detective 🔎
game.tagline: Seven cases. What deserves your attention?
game.doneLine: You marked areas with purpose, chose the right tool for the job, watched behavior develop, and kept only the levels that answer the structural question.

steps.text: A clean chart. Investigate it.

zone.prompt: MARK THE CLEAREST PRIOR SUPPORT AREA.
zone.missHint: Where did the lows keep stopping?

steps.text: Now the other side.

zone.missHint: Where did the highs keep stopping?

levels.name: Find the level
levels.goal: Mark the areas where price repeatedly responded.

debrief.showed: Lows kept stopping in one lower area. Highs kept stopping in one upper area.
debrief.why: Support and resistance are areas where price has repeatedly shown behavior. Not guarantees.

steps.text: Price keeps reacting around one lower area, a few points apart each time.

asks.prompt: Which representation is more useful here?

options.label: Exact reference line
options.feedback: Price reacted across a small area, not one price. A line would make it look like price kept “missing.”

options.label: Reaction zone
options.why: A zone captures the area where price actually responded.

steps.text: New scenario: you need to know whether a candle closes above the prior high at 20,060.

asks.prompt: Which representation is more useful now?

options.label: Exact reference line
options.why: Right. A close-through question needs an exact reference.

options.label: Reaction zone
options.feedback: Here you need one specific price to judge a close against.

levels.name: Line or zone?
levels.goal: Pick the more useful representation for each job.

debrief.showed: A reaction spread across a small area, then a question that needed one exact price.
debrief.why: Zones describe where price behaved. Lines give an exact reference. Use the one the question needs.

steps.text: Price trades up into a resistance area.
A wick above the area. The candle closes back inside.

asks.prompt: Acceptance-like, rejection-like, or not enough information?

options.label: Acceptance-like
options.feedback: No close or hold beyond the area yet.

options.label: Rejection-like
options.feedback: Did price actually move away yet? One wick isn’t much.

steps.text: Price closes above, holds above, pulls back without closing back inside, and pushes higher.

options.label: Acceptance-like
options.why: Closes beyond, holding beyond, structure beyond.

options.label: Rejection-like
options.feedback: Price held above the area.

options.label: Not enough information
options.feedback: Price has shown more now.

levels.name: Accept or reject?
levels.goal: Watch the behavior develop. “Not enough information” is a real answer.

debrief.showed: One wick first (not enough information), then closes, holding and new structure above the area.
debrief.why: Acceptance-like behavior develops over several candles. One wick or one close isn’t the whole story.

steps.text: Four markings on a bullish structure that’s pulling back.

pick.prompt: Structural question: which level would price need to close through to challenge the CURRENT bullish structure?
pick.hint: Which swing is the latest higher low?
pick.why: C, the relevant higher low supporting the current structure.

steps.text: Same chart. A different structural question.

pick.prompt: Which level marks the bottom of the LARGER range price is trading in?
pick.hint: Where did the whole larger structure start?
pick.why: D, the external boundary. A different question gets a different answer.

levels.name: Which level matters more?
levels.goal: The answer depends on the structural question.
levels.readPrompt: Structural question: which level would price need to close through to challenge the CURRENT bullish structure?

debrief.showed: C supports the current bullish structure. D bounds the larger range.
debrief.why: There’s no universal ranking. External isn’t automatically “better.” The question decides which level matters.

steps.text: The structural question: where does the bearish structure stand right now?

clean.prompt: CLEAN THE CHART. Tap every line that doesn’t answer the question.

levels.reason: The external high the bearish structure started from.
levels.name: External high

levels.reason: The lower high capping the current bearish structure.
levels.name: Supporting LH

levels.reason: The prior low price would need to break for bearish continuation.
levels.name: Prior LL

levels.reason: A line through the middle of candles.
A random price inside the move.

levels.name: Delete the junk
levels.goal: Every line left should have a reason.

debrief.showed: Three levels with jobs: the external high, the lower high capping the structure, and the prior low.
debrief.why: If you can’t explain why a line is there, it doesn’t belong on the chart.

steps.text: The previous high is marked.
Price wicks above it and closes below.

asks.prompt: Did price close through the previous high?

options.label: Yes
options.feedback: Look where the body finished.

options.label: No
options.why: A wick through. The close finished back below.

steps.text: Later: price closes above, holds above, and builds structure.

options.label: Acceptance-like
options.why: Close beyond, hold beyond, new structure beyond.

options.label: Rejection-like
options.feedback: Price held above the old high.

options.label: Not enough information
options.feedback: Price has shown a lot here: closes, holding and new structure.

levels.name: What did price do?
levels.goal: Level, then candle behavior, then structure.

debrief.showed: First a wick through and a close back below. Later closes, holding and new structure above.
debrief.why: The landmark didn’t predict anything. Price’s behavior around it told the story.

steps.text: External bullish structure, pulling back. Nine markings.

keep.prompt: YOU CAN ONLY KEEP THREE. Which markings give the clearest structural information for the current analysis?

explain.ext: The external low the whole bullish structure started from: the boundary of the larger range.
explain.sup: The higher low area supporting the current bullish structure. A close through it would challenge the story.
explain.ph: The previous high price would need to overcome for continued bullish progression.

levels.name: Final boss
levels.goal: Real chart-reading practice. Keep only what answers the structural question.

debrief.showed: Three markings carry the structure: the external low, the supporting HL zone, and the previous high.
debrief.why: The FVG, the trendline and the minor levels don’t answer the current structural question. Fewer, better lines.

questionBank.question: Price is approaching a support area that held twice before. What do you know?
options: Price has shown buying interest there before. It doesn’t have to react again
questionBank.why: A level is information, not permission to enter.

questionBank.question: Your friend says, “It’s resistance, so it has to go down.” What’s the flaw?
options: Resistance is an area of interest, not a guaranteed reversal

questionBank.question: Price keeps turning a few points above and below your exact line. Did the level fail?
options: Not necessarily. A zone may describe the reaction better
questionBank.why: Price reacting around a small area isn’t failing.

questionBank.question: Your zone covers 200 points around a reaction that happened within 20. What’s the problem?
options: It’s a giant mystery box that no longer describes the reaction
questionBank.why: Give price room, but keep the zone tied to the reaction.

questionBank.question: Price wicks above resistance, closes back inside, and moves away. What behavior is that?
questionBank.why: Interact, close back inside, move away.

questionBank.question: One candle closes above resistance. Acceptance confirmed?
options: Not yet. Watch whether price holds and builds beyond
Only if the candle is green
questionBank.why: Acceptance-like behavior develops over several candles.

questionBank.question: Price closes above resistance, holds above, and forms a higher low above it. What behavior?
questionBank.why: Close beyond, hold beyond, build beyond.

questionBank.question: Level A: random price, minor reaction. Level B: the relevant swing low with a clear reaction. Which better answers “where is the bullish structure supported?”
A trader says a level has a “93% strength score” because of three touches. What’s wrong?
options: Levels are weighed by context. Touch counts and scores don’t decide it

questionBank.question: Price is approaching a previous high. What does that landmark tell you?
options: Where something structurally meaningful happened before
questionBank.why: Landmarks don’t predict what must happen next.

questionBank.question: Price wicks above a previous high, then closes back below it. Did it close through?
questionBank.why: A wick visited. The close finished back below.

questionBank.question: Which description gives the level a structural job?
options: “This is the swing low supporting the current bullish structure.”
questionBank.why: Name what the level does for the structure.

questionBank.question: Which level would price need to overcome for continued bullish progression?
questionBank.why: The prior high is what continuation has to clear.

questionBank.question: Your chart has 15 lines. What’s the first question for each one?
options: Why is this line here, and what structural question does it answer?
How many touches does it have?
questionBank.why: Every line should have a reason.

questionBank.question: Support, demand, previous swing low and discount all point at the same area. How many areas is that?
options: Possibly one area with four names
questionBank.why: Different frameworks can name overlapping areas differently.

questionBank.question: You understand FVGs, fibs and order blocks. Do they all become entry requirements?
options: No. Knowing a concept ≠ trading the concept
questionBank.why: Market literacy isn’t the same as entry criteria.

What’s the difference between acceptance and rejection?
What makes a level worth keeping on your chart?

final.title: Understanding Structure: Final Quiz
intro: This isn’t just the Section 3 quiz. It’s the mastery gate for all of Phase 2.
You’ll read charts, tap swings, judge breaks, watch behavior at levels and clean up a chart. 16 questions, 80% to pass, unlimited retries with a fresh set.

rounds.prompt: Tap the swing low the latest higher high launched from.
rounds.why: The latest HL. Price launched from it to make the latest HH.

steps.text: The newest swing high is marked “?”.

options.label: HH
options.why: It formed above the previous swing high.

options.label: LH
options.feedback: Compare it to the previous swing high.

options.label: HL
options.feedback: It’s a high, not a low.

options.label: LL
options.feedback: It’s a high, not a low.

steps.text: Price closed below the internal low.

asks.prompt: Did the external bullish structure break?

options.label: No. Only an internal low broke
options.why: The external supporting low is far below.

options.label: Yes, a low broke
options.feedback: Which low? Identify the level first.

steps.text: Price just closed above something.

pick.hint: Which marked high is price now above?
pick.why: B, the relevant prior high. Bullish BOS.

steps.text: Bullish structure. Price closes through the supporting HL.

options.label: Potential bearish MSS
options.why: Against the progression, through the supporting swing.

options.label: Bullish BOS
options.feedback: That break goes against the bullish structure.

options.label: Bearish BOS
options.feedback: The structure was bullish. Breaking against it is change information.

steps.text: Price pulls back and breaks an internal low.

asks.prompt: Continuation, potential shift, or not enough information?

options.label: Continuation
options.feedback: Price hasn’t closed above the prior HH.

options.label: Potential shift
options.feedback: The supporting HL is intact.

steps.text: Look at the last candle.

options.label: Wick through
options.why: It traded above the level and closed back below.

options.label: Close through
options.feedback: Where did the body finish?

steps.text: Watch the last two candles.

options.label: Price moved above the prior high and failed to hold above it
options.why: Observation first.

options.label: Smart money trapped the buyers
options.feedback: The chart can’t show who or why.

options.label: A bullish breakout is confirmed
options.feedback: Price is back below.

steps.text: Price at a resistance area.

asks.prompt: Acceptance-like, rejection-like, or not enough information?

options.label: Acceptance-like
options.why: Closed beyond, held beyond, built beyond.

options.label: Rejection-like
options.feedback: Price stayed above the area.

options.label: Not enough information
options.feedback: Price has shown enough here.

steps.text: Price trades into resistance and keeps going… somewhere.

asks.prompt: What behavior is price showing at the area?

options.label: Rejection-like
options.why: Wicked through, closed back inside, moved away.

options.label: Acceptance-like
options.feedback: Price didn’t hold beyond.

options.label: Not enough information
options.feedback: Price moved away. That’s more information.

steps.text: Question: where does the bullish structure stand right now?

clean.prompt: Delete every line without a structural job.

levels.reason: The higher low supporting the bullish structure.
The prior high continuation would need to clear.

steps.text: Bullish structure, pulling back.

pick.prompt: Which level would price need to close through to challenge the current bullish structure?
pick.hint: Which is the latest higher low?

steps.text: The old HL was closed through. New swings formed.

pick.hint: Which swing is the new move building from?
pick.why: B, the new lower high. Your chart updates because price updates.

options.label: Bullish: higher highs and higher lows
options.why: HL → HH → HL → HH.

options.label: Bearish
options.feedback: Each high and low is higher than the last.

options.label: Range
options.feedback: Price is making progress, not repeating similar highs and lows.

bank.prompt: Previous relevant high: 20,000. New high: 20,050. Previous relevant low: 19,950. New low: 19,980. Label the new swings.

options.label: LH + LL
options.feedback: Compare each new swing to the previous one of the same kind.

options.label: HH + LL
options.feedback: Is 19,980 above or below 19,950?

options.label: LH + HL
options.feedback: Is 20,050 above or below 20,000?

bank.prompt: For hours, price keeps topping near 20,060 and bottoming near 20,000. How would you describe it?

options.label: Consolidating / ranging between similar highs and lows
options.why: Similar highs, similar lows, no sustained progress.

options.label: Bullish progression
options.feedback: No higher highs are forming.

options.label: Bearish progression
options.feedback: No lower lows are forming.

options.label: A reversal
options.feedback: Nothing broke. It’s contained.

bank.prompt: Internal structure turns bearish inside a larger external bullish range. Is the larger structure invalidated?

options.label: Not necessarily
options.why: The furniture can move while the room stays the same.

options.label: Yes, any bearish internal move flips it
options.feedback: Internal swings can turn without breaking the external structure.

options.label: Only if the candles are red
options.feedback: Candle color doesn’t decide structure.

bank.prompt: Bullish structure. Price closes through the HL that supported the latest HH. What does that give you?

options.label: A potential bearish MSS: change information
options.why: Against the progression, through the supporting swing.

options.label: A bullish BOS
options.feedback: That break goes against the bullish structure.

options.label: A confirmed reversal and a short entry
options.feedback: MSS is change information, not an entry signal.

bank.prompt: Bearish structure: LH → LL → LH. Price closes below the relevant prior LL. What is it?

options.label: Bearish BOS: continuation information
options.why: A close through the relevant low, with the structure.

options.label: Bullish MSS
options.feedback: It broke with the bearish structure, not against it.

options.label: A guarantee of more downside
options.feedback: BOS is what price just proved, not what it will do.

bank.prompt: Price drops hard from the HH but never closes through the supporting HL, then forms a new HL. Best description?

options.label: Possible retracement inside the bullish structure
options.why: The supporting swing held.

options.label: Reversal, the move was big
options.feedback: Size and color don’t decide it. Levels do.

options.label: Bearish MSS
options.feedback: The supporting HL wasn’t closed through.

bank.prompt: A candle wicks above the relevant HH and closes back below it. What happened?

options.label: Price traded above it but didn’t finish above it
options.why: A wick can visit.

options.label: A confirmed close-through break
options.feedback: Look where the body finished.

options.label: Nothing at all
options.feedback: Price did trade above it. That’s information.

bank.prompt: Resistance is 20,000. One candle closes at 20,005, the next at 19,985. The most objective description?

options.label: Price moved above the level and failed to hold above it
options.why: Observation before interpretation.

options.label: Big money trapped the buyers
options.feedback: The chart can’t show who traded or why.

options.label: The breakout is confirmed
options.feedback: Price is back below.

bank.prompt: Price closes through the HL supporting your bullish story. Now what?

options.label: Watch what price builds next
options.why: Invalidation ≠ instant opposite bias.

options.label: Short immediately
options.feedback: Invalidation isn’t an entry signal.

options.label: Move the level lower
options.feedback: That ignores what price just did.

options.label: Ignore it
options.feedback: The level holding the story broke.

bank.prompt: One candle closes above resistance. What’s the most accurate read?

options.label: Not enough information yet. Watch whether it holds and builds beyond
options.why: Acceptance-like behavior develops over time.

options.label: Acceptance confirmed
options.feedback: One close is a start, not the whole behavior.

options.label: Rejection-like
options.feedback: Price closed beyond the area.

bank.prompt: Your friend’s chart has 15 lines and she says, “Look at all this confluence.” What should she ask herself first?

options.label: What structural job does each line have?
options.why: Every line should have a reason.

options.label: How can I add more lines?
options.feedback: More markings ≠ more understanding.

options.label: Which line has the most touches?
options.feedback: Touches alone don’t decide it.

bank.prompt: Price is at a support area. Does it have to go up?

options.label: No. A level is information, not permission to enter
options.why: Support is an area of interest.

options.label: Yes
options.feedback: Support ≠ price must go up.

options.label: Only if it’s a zone
options.feedback: Zone or line, it’s still information, not a promise.

bank.prompt: Why can two traders mark different swings on the same chart without one being wrong?

options.label: They may be reading different structural scales or timeframes
options.why: Relevance depends on the structure you’re reading.

options.label: One of them is always wrong
options.feedback: Different scales can make different swings relevant.

options.label: Swings are random
options.feedback: Swings are real turning points.

bank.prompt: Your friend says, “Price broke a low, so it’s bearish now.” What would you check before agreeing?
bank.model: Which low broke (a candle low, a minor internal low, the relevant supporting swing, or the external low), whether price closed through it or only wicked, what the prior structure was, and whether there’s enough information yet. A minor internal break isn’t a bearish structure.

bank.prompt: Pick one level you would keep on a bullish chart and explain its structural job.
bank.model: For example: the higher low supporting the current bullish structure. If price closed through it, the bullish story would be materially challenged. Or the prior high price would need to overcome for continued bullish progression.

reflection.heading: YOU’RE NOT JUST LOOKING AT CANDLES ANYMORE.
reflection.intro:
What you can do now
  • ✓ Identify swing highs and lows
  • ✓ Label HH / HL / LH / LL
  • ✓ Read bullish and bearish structure
  • ✓ Understand internal vs. external structure
  • ✓ Recognize consolidation and expansion
  • ✓ Interpret BOS
  • ✓ Interpret MSS
  • ✓ Distinguish retracement from reversal
  • ✓ Understand wick vs. close
  • ✓ Recognize false breaks
  • ✓ Understand structural invalidation
  • ✓ Identify meaningful levels
  • ✓ Observe acceptance/rejection
  • ✓ Connect levels back to structure
